newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil seen range-bound, currency rules softs.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil seen range-bound, currency rules softs.

text.p: Palm oil is expected to remain in a tight range in the coming week on the European vegetable oil market, traders said.
Although a forecast fall in prices has yet to materialise traders said the market has a downside bias.
Rising output in Malaysia and Indonesia and a slowdown in export business in Malaysia, owing to high prices, is expected to weigh on the market in the coming weeks.
"Malaysian traditional buyers are turning away from palm oil and buying soft oils which are more competitive," said one trader.
"Certainly counties like India, Pakistan and Bangladesh are buying more sunflower oil these days at the expense of palm oil," said another.

On Monday morning Malaysian cargo surveyor Societe General de Surveillance (SGS) released its estimate for local exports for the first 20 days of April. SGS put exports at 429,661 tonnes against 391,599 during March 1-20.
Malaysian private forecaster Ivan Wong in his latest estimate projected an increase in output of six percent over March at 723,000 tonnes.

While not as dramatic as the 35.71 percent increase seen in the Malaysia Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) figures for March, the rise is about in line with expectations and shows a steady build up towards the peak production months of October/November.
Coconut oil came under pressure early last week from increased copra output in Philippines and this trend is expected to continue.
Traders said currency will remain the dominate factor in the soft oils market with the volatile trading in Chicago a background feature.
